notes:
Three real bullets and a nine-row reward table that is not a step of anything -- which reward you get depends on how many of the Abyssea storyline quests you have already done, an outcome the ladder has no business modelling.

The header's giver, Kocchi-Arocchi, never appears in the walkthrough at all; the page opens straight on the Cavernous Maw. He is kept in start because the header is the only thing that names a giver and he does stand at that maw, but nothing in the walkthrough corroborates him, so the quest is demoted to medium rather than pretending the ladder starts on a talk step that the page does not describe.

The traverser stone gate is real and deliberately NOT recorded in items: res/key_items.lua carries six key items all named 'traverser stone' (ids 1271-1276, one per stone you can hold), so the resolver refuses the name outright rather than guess. An unresolvable entry in items would leave step 1 permanently un-ready, which is worse than a note.

Glavoid's zone comes from the quest Description ('has reemerged in Abyssea - Tahrongi'), not from the walkthrough, which gives no location and no pop condition -- so none is invented. Step 3 is unmarkable on purpose: the page says only 'exit', naming neither an exit entity nor a destination.

The [KI] Reive unity is granted at bullet 6, before the final return -- which would make lovely evidence -- but it is also the header's Reward, and hard rule 7 says a reward proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done. It is left off. The cost is one rung of tracking across the walk back to Adoulin; the alternative is a mark that may fire only at completion. Sub-bullets under 5 are fight tactics.

No key item is ever granted and the Medieval Collar is a completion reward, so every step's evidence is null and the runtime will have to lean on the session latch the whole way. That is the honest reading -- there is nothing here to latch onto.

Bullet 10 is a third rung on the same ???. The 18:00-4:00 window on the pop is real and completely invisible to the addon.

notes:
Three bullets, but bullet 2 is not one step -- it is three independent hunts in three different Chains of Promathia zones, and its sub-bullets say exactly where each one is. Modelling it as a single zone-less 'go get three things' step (the Operation Teatime shape) would throw away three zones, seven named drop sources and any marker at all during the longest part of the quest. Instead it becomes three obtain steps sharing a group, since the page imposes no order on them, each carrying its own zone, its own drop mobs and its own item as evidence. Holding the file satisfies one member and leaves the other two drawn, which is precisely the behaviour you want.

The evidence is safe under hard rule 4: three different items on three different steps, and none of them is the reward (4000 gil).

The header's Item Reqs restates the same three items, so nothing there goes unused. 'Windurst Waters South' in the Start field is the south half of zone 238, not a zone -- recorded as Windurst Waters. Taurus count is left null: the page says three can be FOUND at (G-6), not that three must die. Bullet 3's tail ('speak to him again to start the Tuning Out quest') is the next quest, not a step of this one.

notes:
Eight bullets, six of which are 'check the Rhinostery door' -- four in the past and two in the present. The whole quest is one object clicked over and over across two eras, so almost all of the judgement here is about how many rungs that deserves.

Bullets 5, 6 and 7 are MERGED into one step. They are the same door in the same zone at the same grid, separated only by two game-day waits that no packet reports; three rungs the player cannot be tracked through would be noise and the marker never moves between them. Bullet 7 also hands back [KI] "The Healing Herb", which is already step 2's evidence, so hard rule 4 puts it on the earlier step only and the merged step gets none.

That key item's real name carries literal quote marks: res/key_items.lua 957 is "The Healing Herb", quotes included, which is exactly how the page writes it. Without them it does not resolve -- checked.

The target is recorded as 'Rhinostery' because that is the name the page and the Start field actually use; the page never writes a 'Door: ...' form, so inventing one would be guessing at an entity name. Bullet 1's sub-bullet -- two Rhinostery doors, the LEFT one flags the quest -- cannot be expressed in a name or a grid and is kept as a note. Dantie-Corantie and Maju-Naju are cutscene speakers, not entities you interact with, so neither is a target. Bullet 8 is an epilogue after the reward is already paid, marked optional; it takes the key item back off you.

The good part is bullet 2: the page writes 'Door: Acolyte hostel' itself, which is the client's own entity form, so that step carries a real marker instead of pointing vaguely at a building. A zone NPC dump confirms Kipopo is in Southern San d'Oria, so the present-day hop across eras is ground truth rather than inference.

notes:
Four bullets, four steps, all four in one zone -- Marjami Ravine start to finish. The Large strip of Velkk hide is granted at bullet 2 and consumed at bullet 3, and it is not the reward, so it is exactly the kind of clean mid-quest observable that makes a ladder worth having: holding it draws Toppled Tree, not holding it draws the cache.

Two things the schema cannot hold. The route to the Velkk Cache crosses three Colonization Reives that require the Demolishing survival skill, and neither a survival skill nor reive state is in any packet the addon reads -- it is a note. And 'Scalable Area' is a generic target name that exists all over Ulbuka once you have Climbing; this one is pinned only by zone and the K-7/8 border, which is the best the page offers.

The reward line -- gloves, the Climbing skill, 500 Bayld -- is an outcome of bullet 4, not a step. The Start field gives no grid; bullet 1 puts Toppled Tree at (M-7), so that is used for start.grid while start.raw stays verbatim.

notes:
The page is categorised Deprecated and says outright that the original quest can no longer be flagged -- it was removed on 27 March 2012. There is no numbered walkthrough left, just two prose paragraphs describing what the NPC does NOW: speak to Hildolf, he asks for a vial of Slime Oil, you bring it, you pick a Fewell element and he crafts it. That is what the ladder records, because it is the only thing a player can actually do at this quest's giver today.

The header is stale in exactly the way the pilot warned about: Item Reqs still lists Earth Crystal, Flint Stone, Mythril Sand and Brass Tank, all four belonging to the removed version, and none of them is used anywhere in the text. They are deliberately NOT recorded as items -- gating a step on four things the game no longer wants would stall the ladder forever.

Bullet 1 is not a step. 'Speak to a Synergy Engineer to obtain a Synergy Crucible' is a workaround for players who missed the flag window, not part of this quest; Synergy Engineer is also a generic name shared by many NPCs across several zones, so it could not carry a marker anyway. The [KI] Synergy crucible is the header Reward, so hard rule 7 keeps it out of evidence, and there is no other observable in the quest. The sub-bullet about the log entry completing with Synergistic Support is an outcome. Medium, not high: the ladder describes live NPC behaviour that the page itself says may not correspond to a flaggable quest at all.

notes:
Bullet 1 is a genuine step and not a precondition: you must open your permanent key items and examine the [KI] Carrier pigeon letter before Carmelo will give you the quest. It has no location and nothing to click, so it is deliberately unmarkable -- but it keeps the rung and it is where the Carrier pigeon letter requirement belongs. Its evidence is null because the key item was granted by The Stars of Ifrit, not here; hard rule 3 is explicit about that.

The header's Previous lists both The Siren's Tear and The Stars of Ifrit, and both are recorded, but the page softens both: the sub-bullets say you need only the key item from The Stars of Ifrit and not its completion, and that an active Siren's Tear merely changes Carmelo's prompt. Neither nuance has a slot in gates.

The page contradicts itself on the target's name -- the Description says you throw the sheet into 'the Mirror Lake', the walkthrough says click 'Mirror Pond'. The walkthrough is the one giving the instruction, so Mirror Pond is what is recorded. Its weather gate (only on days without snow or clouds; 'Gloom' with sun is fine) is invisible to the addon. Carmelo's song sheet is the header's Item Reqs and is what you must be holding at the pond, so it is real items and clean evidence one step earlier -- the best-tracked part of the quest.

notes:
Eight bullets into seven steps. Bullets 5 and 6 merge: the same ??? in North Gustaberg (S) at (J-4), clicked twice with nothing in between, the second click giving the [KI] unadorned ring. That key item is granted mid-quest and is not the reward (Trainee Burin), so it is the quest's one clean observable and it lands on the merged step.

The giver is written 'Wahid (S)' in the header and plain 'Wahid' in the walkthrough. The (S) form is kept, exactly as the guide says to keep Abyssea's (A) form: the normaliser folds it to both 'wahid [s]' and 'wahid', so it matches whichever the live entity is called, while the bare form would match only one. Checked against the resolver.

Bullet 4 is a step, not scenery: you have to zone out to North Gustaberg (S) to get the cutscene, and its sub-bullet is a way to tell the right cutscene from the wrong one -- a soldier called Bernhard talking about a scream near Palborough Mines -- which cannot be modelled and stays a note. Bullet 7's step keeps items empty: you are carrying the unadorned ring, but the page never calls it a trade and Under Oath's last step sets the precedent for a key item taken in conversation. Both 'leave the zone and come back' bullets are real waits with nothing observable in them.
